chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Wasshash, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Do not reap at night, and do not harvest at night, and do not sacrifice at night, and do not sow at night, for if you do, the satisfied one and the passer-by will not come to you."

I asked: 'And what are the satisfied one and the passer-by?' He said: 'The satisfied one is the one who is content with what you gave him, and the passer-by is the one who passes by you and asks you.'

And if you harvest at night, the beggar will not come to you. This is the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And give their due on the day of its harvest.' At the time of harvest, he means the collection (of zakat) after the collection (of the crop), when you have harvested it.

And when it is taken out, it is the handful after the handful. And similarly at the time of threshing, and similarly for sowing: do not sow at night, because you give in sowing as you give in harvesting."

key_terms.الصِّرَامُ: Threshing (the process of separating grain from chaff)
key_terms.الْحَفْنَةَ: The handful (referring to the measure or portion given)
key_terms.الْقَانِعُ: The satisfied one (one who is content with a small amount of charity)
key_terms.وَالْمُعْتَرُّ: The passer-by (one who stops to ask/beg)

ai.seo_question: Why should zakat be paid during the day rather than at night according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the timing of zakat distribution to the practical maximization of charity, explaining that daytime payments allow for the inclusion of the 'satisfied one' (who accepts modest amounts) and the 'passer-by' (who asks for help), whereas night payments may limit these opportunities. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *maslahah* (public interest) and the social dimensions of purification, connecting the ritual act to the Quranic principle of giving the due share specifically at the time of harvest (7:155).
